### 1 — Scene
A mixed vegetarian-style meal: tofu-like slices, a red seasoned grain mixture, and shredded vegetable slaw.

### 2 — Vessel
A large, rounded-square dinner plate, partly cropped. I estimate an effective diameter of **27 cm** for the area calculation:
**3.14 × 13.5² ≈ 572 cm²**.

### 3 — Items
- Firm tofu slices with herbs and a few vegetable pieces.
- Red seasoned quinoa-like grains with cooked vegetables and sauce.
- Shredded cabbage/radish slaw with carrot and other vegetables, lightly dressed.

Any visible sauce or dressing is included in the corresponding item's energy density; there is no clearly separate pool of oil.

### 4–7 — Area, volume, weight, and energy
These are estimates of the visible food only.

| Item | Plate area | Area | Average height | Gross volume | Bulk density | Weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Tofu and herbs | 14% | 80 cm² | 1.4 cm | 112 ml | 0.95 g/ml | 106 g | 150 | 159 kcal |
| Seasoned quinoa and vegetables | 17% | 97 cm² | 1.9 cm | 185 ml | 0.8 g/ml | 148 g | 155 | 229 kcal |
| Dressed vegetable slaw | 17% | 97 cm² | 1.3 cm | 126 ml | 0.6 g/ml | 76 g | 55 | 42 kcal |

The area shares total **48%**, leaving roughly half the plate bare. Gross volumes are reduced only by the stated bulk densities.

### 8 — Sanity check
Approximately **330 g and 430 kcal** is plausible for these three modest piles on a partly empty dinner plate. The main uncertainties are the identity of the sliced protein and the amount of oil in the grains and dressing.
